A generic reader of **located event feeds** for Gladys Assistant: paste the address of up to five
feeds (USGS earthquakes, GDACS alerts, NSW Rural Fire Service fires, the feed of a local
authority…), and Gladys follows the events within a radius of your house, shows them on the
dashboard and starts a scene when one appears or disappears.

Formats read: **GeoJSON** (`FeatureCollection`), **GeoRSS** (Simple and GML), **W3C geo**
(`geo:lat` / `geo:long`), **RSS 2.0**, **RSS 1.0** and **Atom**.

For worldwide disasters or European earthquakes, the dedicated integrations
[GDACS](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-gdacs) and [EMSC](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-emsc)
know their sources better (alert levels, magnitude revisions): this one is for any other feed.

A complement, not a safety alert system: follow the instructions of your local authorities.

## What you get

- One **device per feed**: the number of events in the area, the distance and title of the
  nearest one, the latest event in words, and a badge telling whether the feed can be read.
- A **dashboard widget**: the current events of each feed, then the nearest ones.
- Two **scene triggers**: a new event in the area, an event removed.
- A **scene action** that reads the events of your area as one sentence.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.1.0 or later.
- Internet access from Gladys (the feeds are read by the integration container).
- The location of your house in Gladys (Settings → Houses), or coordinates typed in the
  configuration. Without either, only feeds with the radius "Whole feed" work.
- The address of a public feed. A few that work:
  - USGS earthquakes of the last day:
    `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/2.5_day.geojson`
  - GDACS disaster alerts: `https://www.gdacs.org/xml/rss.xml`
  - NSW Rural Fire Service major incidents: `https://www.rfs.nsw.gov.au/feeds/majorIncidents.json`

## Configuration

### Settings

For each of the five feeds:

| Setting                     | Use                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Feed address                | http or https, 5 MB at most. Empty: the slot is not used.                               |
| Name                        | Shown in the widget and the scenes. Empty: "Geo feed 1 (host)".                         |
| Radius                      | Distance from the centre to the event. "Whole feed": every event, for a local feed.     |
| Categories (optional)       | Keep only the events whose category contains one of these words (commas between words). |
| Numeric property (optional) | A numeric property of the events, `mag` for the USGS: sent to the scenes as `value`.    |
| Minimum value (optional)    | Events whose property is lower, or missing, are ignored.                                |

Then, for every feed:

- **Centre latitude / longitude**: empty, the location of your house.
- **Refresh interval**: 5 to 60 minutes.
- **Maximum age of the events**: older events are ignored; events without a readable date are
  kept.
- **Language of the texts**: names of the devices and features at their creation, texts sent to
  the scenes.

Save, then open the **Discover** tab and create the devices.

### Reading a feed

- **GeoJSON**: a Point is used as it is; for a Polygon, MultiPolygon or line, the centre of its
  points; for a GeometryCollection, its first Point (NSW RFS sends the fire point and its area).
- The identifier is `id` or `guid`; without one, a digest of the title, link and position.
- Title: `title`, `name`, `headline` or `place`. Date: `time`, `date`, `pubDate`, `published`,
  `updated`. Category: `category` or `type`. Link: `url` or `link`.
- **RSS and Atom**: `georss:point`, `georss:polygon`, `georss:box`, `gml:pos` or `geo:lat` /
  `geo:long`; title, link, `guid` or `id`, `pubDate` or `updated`, `category`. Items without a
  position are skipped.
- Nothing of a feed is ever run: it is only read. The XML DOCTYPE is ignored.

## Device

One device per feed, refreshed by the integration itself (no Gladys polling):

| Feature                | Type         | Value                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Events in the area     | counter      | Followed events of the feed.                                             |
| Nearest event distance | distance, km | The nearest followed event; 20,038 km (the farthest possible) when none. |
| Nearest event          | text         | Its title.                                                               |
| Latest event           | text         | The newest followed event, with its distance.                            |

The device **badge** shows "Cloud" when the last reading worked, "Unreachable" otherwise; the
reason (no answer, HTTP error, not a feed…) is in the integration status and the widget.

## Dashboard widget

**Geo feed events**: a heading with the number of events, one row per feed (its count, or why it
cannot be read), the nearest events (8 at most) with their feed and distance, and the time of the
last reading. Tap an event: its summary, its date and a link to it. The settings choose the feeds
to show (empty: all).

## Scene triggers

**Geo feed: new event in the area**: an event enters the followed set of a feed (radius, age,
categories and minimum value). **Geo feed: event removed**: a followed event leaves the feed, or
no longer matches (too old, moved away).

The first reading of a feed, and the first one after a configuration change, fire nothing: what
is there is the starting point. A restart fires nothing either (the followed events are kept in
`/data`). At most 20 events per feed and per reading.

Filter: the feed (empty: any). Variables:

| Variable      | Content                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `feed_name`   | The name of the feed.                                        |
| `title`       | The title of the event.                                      |
| `category`    | Its categories, separated by commas.                         |
| `distance_km` | Distance from the centre, empty without a centre.            |
| `value`       | The numeric property chosen for the feed, empty without one. |
| `time`        | The date of the event (ISO 8601), empty if unknown.          |
| `url`         | The link of the event.                                       |
| `summary`     | Title and distance, ready for a message.                     |
| `latitude`    | Latitude of the event.                                       |
| `longitude`   | Longitude of the event.                                      |
| `properties`  | The simple properties of the event, as JSON.                 |

## Scene action

**Geo feed: read the events** reads the feeds again if needed and answers with `text` (the events
as one sentence, nearest first), `count` and `nearest_km` (20038 when there is none). The feed
filter limits it to one feed. The **Read the feeds now** button of the configuration tells, feed
by feed, what was read.

## Scene examples

- **Earthquake nearby**: trigger "new event in the area" on the USGS feed (radius 250 km,
  property `mag`, minimum 4) → send a message "\{\{summary\}\}, magnitude \{\{value\}\}".
- **Bushfire warning**: NSW RFS feed, categories `Watch and Act, Emergency`, radius 50 km →
  turn on a light in red and send the link `{{url}}`.
- **Morning briefing**: every day at 7:30, action "read the events" → read `text` aloud.

## Data sources, terms and quotas

The data belong to the publisher of each feed: read and respect its terms of use, and credit it
when you share them. The USGS feeds are in the public domain
([earthquake.usgs.gov](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/)), GDACS asks to be cited.
The integration reads each feed at most every 5 minutes, with its own User-Agent, and reads 5 MB
at most: enough for public feeds, which are mostly refreshed every 5 to 15 minutes.

## Troubleshooting

- **"not a GeoJSON, RSS or Atom feed"**: the address gives a web page. Look for the feed link
  (GeoJSON, RSS, Atom) on the site of the publisher.
- **No event while the feed has some**: check the radius and the location of your house, the
  categories and the minimum value; a property that the events do not have excludes them all.
- **"No centre"**: give your house a location in Gladys or type coordinates.
- **The dates are missing** (NSW RFS): the feed gives local dates without a time zone; they are
  not guessed. The maximum age keeps these events.
- Logs: `docker logs` of the integration container; `LOG_LEVEL=debug` shows each reading.

## Limits

- Five feeds at most; one radius and filters per feed.
- The distance is measured to the centre of an area, not to its edge: a large area around your
  house can be farther than the radius.
- No authentication: public feeds only (a token in the query string works, and is never logged).
- Not affiliated with the USGS, GDACS, NSW RFS nor any feed publisher.

## How to install GeoJSON & GeoRSS feeds in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: GeoJSON & GeoRSS feeds appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-geofeeds:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-geofeeds](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-geofeeds).

GeoJSON & GeoRSS feeds requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

GeoJSON & GeoRSS feeds is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
